parameters.general.opacity.description: Layers can overwrite basic parameters and exert force fields. The opacity is specified with this parameter between 0 and 1. A value of 1 means that parameters in the core area of the layer can be completely overwritten, while a value of 0 means that the layer has no effect.
parameters.general.share.name: Relative strength
parameters.general.share.description: Energy that cells release, for example through radiation, energy costs or decay, is emitted as energy particles. A part of them is created directly next to the cell, the rest in the radiation sources. This parameter determines the fraction that is created in this radiation source. It also scales the external energy inflow for this source. The relative strengths of all radiation sources and of the base add up to 1.

parameters.visualization.name: Visualization
parameters.energy.name: Guided energy supply
parameters.visualization.backgroundcolor: Color of the empty background of the world. A layer is only tinted with its background color if it is activated. Otherwise, the layer leaves the background unchanged apart from the height map of its force field.
parameters.visualization.customizationco: Defines the 10 customization colors. They are used to render the objects and appear in all color selections.
Here, one can set how the objects are to be colored during rendering. The brightness always follows the energy of the object.

 Energy: No own color is used, so the objects are displayed in grayscale. The more energy an object has, the brighter it is.

 Customization: Each object is displayed in its customization color.

 Lineage + Customization: Like 'Customization', but the hue is shifted slightly depending on the lineage. Creatures of the same lineage therefore keep a common basic color and can still be distinguished.

 Lineage: Each lineage is assigned its own color.

 Creature: Each creature is assigned its own color.

The last three options evaluate the creature of a cell. All other objects are displayed in their customization color.
parameters.visualization.glow.name: Glow
parameters.visualization.glow.descriptio: Controls the bloom effect intensity. At 0, no glow is applied. At 1, maximum glow is applied.
parameters.visualization.fluidilluminati: With hardware ray tracing, the cells light the surrounding fluids in their colors. This parameter controls the strength of this light. At 0, the fluids are not lit by the cells. At 1, they are lit most strongly.
parameters.visualization.borderlessrende: If activated, the simulation is rendered periodically in the view port.
parameters.visualization.gridlines.name: Grid lines
parameters.visualization.gridlines.descr: This option draws a suitable grid in the background depending on the zoom level.
parameters.visualization.markreferencedo: This option draws a frame around the reference domain of the world. It is helpful with borderless rendering, where the world is repeated periodically in the view port.
parameters.visualization.sourceshowradia: If activated, the area of the radiation source is highlighted in the background.
parameters.visualization.sourcelightcolo: Color of the light of the radiation source. The highlighted area of the radiation source takes this color as well.
parameters.visualization.sourcelightbrig: With hardware ray tracing, the area of the radiation source shines. Its light illuminates the objects and fluids around it and appears as columns of light in a faint haze. The objects on the way cast shadows, which become softer the farther they fall. This parameter sets the brightness that the light approaches close to the source. At 0, the source does not shine.
parameters.visualization.sourcelightrang: Distance from the area of the radiation source up to which its light reaches. The light fades out smoothly towards this distance.
parameters.visualization.layershowforcef: If activated, the background color of the layer is darkened according to the height map of its force field. The higher the value in the height map, the darker the background.
parameters.energy.externalenergy.name: External energy amount
parameters.energy.externalenergy.descrip:
This parameter can be used to set the amount of energy of an external energy pool. This energy can then be transferred to constructor cells and radiation sources (see the inflow settings).

Warning: Too much external energy can result in a massive production of cells and slow down or even crash the simulation.
parameters.energy.externalenergyinflowfo:
The maximum amount of energy that is transferred from the external energy pool to a constructor cell each time it tries to build a new cell.

If the external energy pool cannot satisfy all requesting constructor cells, the available energy is distributed proportionally.
parameters.energy.externalenergyinflowth:
Here one can specify the fraction of energy that constructor cells must provide by themselves before constructing with external energy inflow.

For example, a value of 0.6 means that a constructor cell needs energy amounting to at least 60% of the energy required to build the new cell by itself. Otherwise, no external energy inflow is requested.
parameters.energy.externalenergyinflowon:
If activated, external energy can only be transferred to constructor cells that have not yet produced any offspring. This option can be used to limit the external energy supply. Constructors that build parts of their own creature are not restricted.

The setting is evaluated for the customization color of the cell with the constructor.
parameters.energy.externalenergyinflowfo:
The absolute amount of energy that is transferred from the external energy pool to the radiation sources in each time step. Each color entry defines the energy that is emitted in the corresponding color.

Each radiation source receives these amounts multiplied by its relative strength and emits them as energy particles. If the external energy pool does not contain enough energy, only the remaining energy is distributed.
parameters.energy.externalenergybackflow: The proportion of energy that flows back from the simulation to the external energy pool. Each time an object releases energy, for example through radiation, energy costs or decay, this fraction is taken. The remaining fraction stays in the simulation as a new energy particle.
Energy from the simulation can only flow back into the external energy pool as long as the amount of external energy is below this value.
parameters.shape.name: Shape
parameters.forcefield.name: Force field
parameters.shape.layershape.name: Shape
parameters.shape.layershape.description:
Geometric shape of the layer.
 Circular: the core is a disc around the center.
 Rectangular: the core is a rectangle around the center.
parameters.shape.layercoreradius.name: Core radius
parameters.shape.layercoreradius.descrip: Radius of the core area in which the layer takes full effect.
parameters.shape.layercorerect.name: Core size (width,height)
parameters.shape.layercorerect.descripti: Width and height of the core area in which the layer takes full effect.
parameters.shape.layerfadeoutradius.name: Fade-out radius
parameters.shape.layerfadeoutradius.desc: Width of the border area around the core in which the effect of the layer fades out to zero.
parameters.shape.sourceshapetype.name: Shape
parameters.shape.sourceshapetype.descrip:
Geometric shape of the area in which the energy particles of this source are created.
 Circular: a disc around the center.
 Rectangular: a rectangle around the center.
parameters.shape.sourcecircularradius.de: Radius of the area in which the energy particles are created.
parameters.shape.sourcerectangularrect.d: Width and height of the area in which the energy particles are created.
parameters.forcefield.layerforcefieldtyp:
Force field that the layer exerts on all objects and energy particles inside it.
 None: no force field.
 Radial: the objects circle around the center of the layer.
 Central: the objects are drawn towards the center of the layer.
 Linear: a constant force acts in one direction.
 Perlin noise: a noise field generates a turbulent flow that changes over time.
parameters.forcefield.layerradialforcefi:
Direction of rotation of the radial force field.
 Clockwise
 Counter clockwise
Strength of the rotational force around the center of the layer.
Rotates the force away from the tangential direction. At 0 the objects only circle around the center, other values additionally pull them inwards or outwards.
parameters.forcefield.layercentralforcef: Strength of the force towards the center of the layer. The force is weak directly at the center, reaches its maximum a short distance away and decreases again further out.
parameters.forcefield.layerlinearforcefi: Direction in which the force acts.
Strength of the force. It is the same everywhere in the core area of the layer.
parameters.forcefield.layerperlinnoisefo: Strength of the force that is derived from the noise field.
Size of the spatial structures of the noise field. Larger values produce larger vortices.
Number of time steps after which the noise field is completely renewed. Larger values let it change more slowly.

parameters.motion.timestepsize.name: Time step size
parameters.motion.timestepsize.descripti: The time duration calculated in a single simulation step. Smaller values increase the accuracy of the simulation while larger values can lead to numerical instabilities.
parameters.motion.smoothinglength.name: Smoothing length
parameters.motion.smoothinglength.descri: The smoothing length determines the region of influence of the neighboring particles for the calculation of density, pressure and viscosity. Values that are too small lead to numerical instabilities, while values that are too large cause the particles to drift apart.
parameters.motion.pressurestrength.name: Pressure
parameters.motion.pressurestrength.descr: Strength of the pressure that pushes neighboring objects apart.
parameters.motion.viscositystrength.name: Viscosity
parameters.motion.viscositystrength.desc: Strength of the viscosity. Larger values lead to a smoother movement.
parameters.motion.friction.name: Friction
parameters.motion.friction.description: This specifies the fraction of the velocity that is slowed down per time step.
parameters.motion.innerfriction.name: Inner friction
parameters.motion.innerfriction.descript: Fraction of the relative velocity along a connection by which two connected objects are slowed down per time step.
parameters.motion.rigidity.name: Rigidity of solids
parameters.motion.rigidity.description: A higher value will cause connected objects in solids to move more uniformly as a rigid body.
parameters.thresholds.maxvelocity.name: Maximum velocity
parameters.thresholds.maxvelocity.descri: Maximum velocity that an object can reach.
parameters.thresholds.maxforce.name: Maximum force
parameters.thresholds.maxforce.descripti: Maximum force that can act on an object without breaking its connections. If the force is exceeded, the object loses all its connections with a certain probability.
Minimum distance between two objects. Objects that come closer are pushed apart.
parameters.thresholds.maxbindingdistance: Maximum length of a connection between two objects. Longer connections break.
parameters.thresholds.objectfusionveloci: Minimum relative velocity of two colliding objects at which they form a new connection. At least one of the two objects must be sticky and both must have a free connection slot.
parameters.radiation.relativestrengthbas: Energy that cells release, for example through radiation, energy costs or decay, is emitted as energy particles. A part of them is created directly next to the cell, the rest in the radiation sources. This parameter determines the fraction that is created next to the cell. Together with the relative strengths of all radiation sources it adds up to 1.
parameters.radiation.disableradiationsou: If activated, all radiation sources within this layer are deactivated.
parameters.radiation.radiationabsorption: The fraction of energy that a cell can absorb from an incoming energy particle can be specified here.
parameters.radiation.radiationtype1stren: Fraction of its energy that a cell emits on average per time step in the form of energy particles as soon as its age exceeds the minimum age of radiation type I.
parameters.radiation.radiationtype1minim: Age in time steps from which a cell emits energy particles through radiation type I.
parameters.radiation.radiationtype2stren: Fraction of its energy that a cell emits on average per time step in the form of energy particles as long as its energy exceeds the threshold of radiation type II.
parameters.radiation.radiationtype2energ: Energy above which a cell emits energy particles through radiation type II. Usable and raw energy are considered separately.
parameters.radiation.particlesplitenergy: The minimum energy of an energy particle after which it can split into two particles, whereby it receives a small momentum. The splitting does not occur immediately, but only after a certain time.
parameters.radiation.sourceradiationangl: If activated, all energy particles of this source fly in this direction. Otherwise they fly away from the center of the source.
parameters.lifecycle.name: Cell life cycle
parameters.construction.name: Cell construction
parameters.mutations.name: Mutations
parameters.lifecycle.maxcellage.name: Maximum age
parameters.lifecycle.maxcellage.descript: Defines the maximum age of a cell. If a cell exceeds this age, it changes to the state 'Dying' and then disintegrates with the decay rate of dying cells.
parameters.lifecycle.freecellmaxage.name: Maximum free cell age
parameters.lifecycle.freecellmaxage.desc: Maximum age of free cells (cells that arise from energy particles). Older free cells disintegrate into energy particles.
parameters.lifecycle.mincellenergy.name: Minimum energy
parameters.lifecycle.mincellenergy.descr: Minimum energy a cell needs to exist. If its usable energy falls below this value, the cell changes to the state 'Dying'. Free cells with less energy disintegrate with the decay rate of dying cells.
parameters.lifecycle.normalcellenergy.de:
The normal energy value of a cell is defined here. This is used as a reference value in various contexts: 

 Energy flow: A cell that does not need energy itself passes everything above the normal value on to a connected cell that is still building.

 Depot cells: Only the energy above the normal value can be moved into the storage of the depot.

 Constructor: Creating new cells costs energy. The creation of new cells is executed only when the residual energy of the constructor does not fall below the normal value.

 If the transformation of energy particles into free cells is activated, an energy particle transforms into a free cell as soon as its energy reaches the normal value.
parameters.lifecycle.celldeathprobabilit:
The probability per time step with which a cell will disintegrate (i.e. transform into an energy particle) when it is in the state 'Dying'. This can occur when one of the following conditions is satisfied:

 The cell has too low energy.

 The cell has exceeded its maximum age.

 The cell has lost the connection to the head cell of its creature.

Free cells with too low energy disintegrate with the same probability.
parameters.lifecycle.particletransformat: If activated, an energy particle transforms into a free cell as soon as its energy reaches the normal energy value.
parameters.construction.constructorconne: When a constructor starts building a new branch, it checks whether the connection to the first new cell would cross existing connections of objects within this distance. In this case, the construction is postponed.
parameters.mutations.newlineagethreshold: As soon as the accumulated mutations of a creature exceed this value, the creature is given a new lineage id and the counter is reset.
parameters.metamproperties.neuronsmetamu: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the neuron mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamproperties.connectionsme: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the connection mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamproperties.celltypeprope: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the cell type property mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamproperties.constructorme: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the constructor mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamproperties.geometrymetam: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the geometry mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamidentity.celltypemetamut: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the cell type mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamidentity.celltypemodemet: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the cell type mode mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamidentity.voidmetamutatio: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the void mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamidentity.customizationme: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the customization mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamidentity.customizationtr: Determines which customizations a customization mutation may produce. Row = old customization, column = new one.

parameters.metamidentity.name: Meta-mutations: Cell identity
parameters.metamgene.addnodemetamutation: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the add node mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamgene.deletenodemetamutat: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the delete node mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamgene.extendgenemetamutat: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the extend gene mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamgene.trimgenemetamutatio: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the trim gene mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamgene.copynodesectionmeta: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the copy node section mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamgene.movenodesectionmeta: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the move node section mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamgenome.addgenemetamutati: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the add gene mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamgenome.duplicategenemeta: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the duplicate gene mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.
parameters.metamgenome.deletegenemetamut: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the probability of the delete gene mutations stored in a genome. It only acts on genomes for which 'Apply meta-mutations' is enabled, and is applied once per offspring.

parameters.attacker.attackerenergycost.d: Amount of energy that an attacker cell loses per attack attempt in the form of emitted energy particles.
parameters.attacker.attackerfoodchaincol:
This matrix can be used to determine how well one cell can attack another cell. The color of the attacking cell corresponds to the row number and the color of the attacked cell to the column number. A value of 0 means that the attacked cell cannot be digested, i.e. no energy can be obtained. A value of 1 means that the maximum energy can be obtained in the digestion process.

Example: If a zero is entered in row 2 and column 3, it means that cells with the second customization color cannot attack cells with the third one.
parameters.attacker.attackerstrength.des: Fraction of the energy of a target that an attacker cell drains per time step. The amount is further reduced by defender cells, the food chain color matrix and the protection parameters.
parameters.attacker.attackerrelatedlinea: Fraction by which the stolen energy is reduced when the attacked creature belongs to the same lineage.
parameters.attacker.attackersizeprotecti: If the attacked creature consists of more cells than the attacking creature, the obtained energy is reduced by this fraction. This compensates for the systematic advantage smaller creatures would otherwise have.
parameters.attacker.attackerradius.name: Attack radius
parameters.attacker.attackerradius.descr: The maximum distance over which an attacker cell can attack another cell.
parameters.digestor.maxrawenergyconducti: Upper limit for the raw energy that a digestor cell can take in from a connected cell or pass on to a connected digestor cell. It scales the digestor property 'Energy conductivity'.
parameters.digestor.maxrawenergyconversi: Upper limit for the raw energy that a digestor cell can convert into usable energy per time step. It scales the digestor property 'Energy conversion'.
parameters.defender.defenderantiattacker: If an attacked cell is a defender cell in anti-attacker mode or is connected to such cells, the stolen energy is divided by (1 + this value) for each of these defender cells.
parameters.defender.defenderantiinjector: If the target cell of an injector is connected to defender cells in anti-injector mode, the energy cost of the injection increases by this fraction for each of these defender cells.
parameters.injector.injectorenergycost.d: Amount of energy an injector cell loses per successful injection in the form of emitted energy particles. Every defender cell in anti-injector mode that is connected to the target increases the cost.
parameters.injector.injectorradius.name: Injection radius
parameters.injector.injectorradius.descr: The maximum distance over which an injector cell can infect another cell.
parameters.muscle.muscleenergycost.name: Energy cost
parameters.muscle.muscleenergycost.descr: Determines how much energy a muscle cell loses in the form of emitted energy particles when it acts. The amount scales with the activation.
parameters.muscle.musclemovementaccelera: Strength of the acceleration of a muscle cell that moves itself directly. It scales with the activation. This parameter applies only to muscle cells in 'Direct movement' mode.
parameters.muscle.musclecrawlingaccelera: Strength of the acceleration that a muscle cell generates while it changes the length of its connection. This parameter applies only to muscle cells in 'Auto crawling' or 'Manual crawling' mode.
parameters.muscle.musclebendingaccelerat: Strength of the acceleration that a muscle cell generates during a bending action. This parameter applies only to muscle cells in 'Auto bending' or 'Manual bending' mode.
parameters.sensor.sensorradius.name: Radius
parameters.sensor.sensorradius.descripti: Upper limit for the radius in which a sensor cell can scan. The scan range of an individual sensor cell is additionally restricted by its own maximum range.
parameters.reconnector.reconnectorradius: The maximum distance at which a reconnector cell can establish connections to other objects.
parameters.detonator.detonatorradius.des: Radius within which the explosion of a detonator cell pushes away surrounding objects. The subsequent shock wave reaches eight times further.
parameters.detonator.detonatorchainexplo: The probability that the explosion of one detonator will trigger the explosion of other detonators within the blast radius.
parameters.colortransition.colortransiti: Rules can be defined that describe how the colors of cells will change over time. For this purpose, a subsequent color can be defined for each customization color. In addition, durations must be specified that define how many time steps the corresponding color is kept. The age of the cell is reset with each color change.

genome.attribute.genomename: Name of the genome. Every creature that is built from it inherits the name.
genome.attribute.genomefrontangle: Angle between the first connection of the head cell and the front direction of the creature. From the head cell the front direction is propagated to all other cells.
genome.attribute.genomeresistancetoinjec: If enabled, injector cells cannot overwrite the genome of creatures built from it.
genome.attribute.genomeapplymetamutation: If enabled, the mutation rates of this genome are themselves mutated. The step sizes come from the 'Meta-mutations' groups in the simulation parameters.

neural.title: Neural network
neural.preview.detailed: Activates a more detailed simulation including signals and muscles
neural.preview.showactivity: Shows the neural activity editor in the preview
node.attribute.nodeangle: Angle of this cell relative to the connection to the previous cell. It is only evaluated for the first and the last node of a gene; for inner nodes the angle results from the selected shape.
node.attribute.nodecustomization: Customization color of the cell. Many simulation parameters are defined per color.
node.attribute.celltype:
Function that the cell performs after its neural network has been executed.
 Base: No special function. Only the neural network is evaluated.
 Depot: Stores usable energy and releases it again on demand. A positive signal in channel #0 stores energy, a negative one releases it.
 Sensor: Scans the environment and reports direction, distance and mass of a match.
 Generator: Generates a periodic signal.
 Attacker: Steals energy from free cells or from cells of other creatures.
 Injector: Injects its own genome into a foreign cell that has a constructor.
 Muscle: Generates movement by bending connections, changing their length or accelerating the cell directly.
 Defender: Protects its creature against attacker or injector cells of other creatures.
 Reconnector: Establishes or removes connections to other objects.
 Detonator: Explodes after a countdown and pushes away surrounding objects.
 Digestor: Converts raw energy into usable energy and conducts it to other digestor cells.
 Memory: Delays, records, stores or smooths the signal.
 Communicator: Transmits the signal to communicator cells of other creatures.
 Void: Dissolves immediately after the cell network is finished and passes its energy to the neighboring cells. Serves as temporary scaffolding for constructing complex shapes.
node.attribute.nodeconstructiongene: Gene that this cell builds as a constructor. 'None' means that the cell has no constructor.
node.attribute.constructorautotriggerint: If set, the constructor triggers itself every n time steps, with a phase that differs per creature. Without a value it has to be triggered via channel #0.
node.attribute.constructorconstructionan: Angle by which the first constructed cell deviates from the middle of the largest gap between the connections of the constructor cell. It is only evaluated for the first cell of the first concatenation in the first branch.
node.attribute.constructorprovideenergy:
Determines how much energy the constructor cell raises for a construction.
 Cell only: only the energy of the constructed cell itself.
 Transitive cells: additionally the energy reserve of a constructed constructor cell, unless that constructor references the first gene. The reserve covers the cells of the gene that constructor references, or every cell reachable from it if that constructor also uses 'Transitive cells', so they can be built without further energy.
 Free: cells are built without energy cost. The setting falls back to 'Cell only' after the first completed offspring and cannot be used in a genome.
node.attribute.constructorseparation: If enabled, the offspring detaches from the constructor cell after the last cell has been built.
node.attribute.constructornumbranches: Number of cell networks that the constructor builds next to each other from the same gene.
node.attribute.constructornumconcatenati: How often the gene is built in a row, each attached to the previous one.
node.attribute.depotstoragelimit: Maximum usable energy that the depot can store.
node.attribute.sensorautotrigger: If enabled, the sensor scans in every cycle. Otherwise it only scans when channel #0 exceeds the trigger threshold.
node.attribute.sensortagforattackers: If enabled, attacker cells of the same creature in 'Creature' mode may attack the creatures this sensor detects in 'Detect creature' mode. These are the match and up to 3 further matching creatures near the match. Only the scan of the current cycle counts.
node.attribute.sensormode:
Selects what the sensor scans for.
 Detect energy: searches for accumulations of energy particles.
 Detect solid: searches for solid particles.
 Detect free cell: searches for accumulations of free cells.
 Detect creature: searches for cells of other creatures.
node.attribute.sensorenergymindensity: Minimum density of energy particles that is required for a match. The value lies between 0 and 1.
node.attribute.sensorfreecellmindensity: Minimum density of free cells that is required for a match. The value lies between 0 and 1.
node.attribute.sensorrestricttocolors: Only objects with one of the selected customization colors are detected.
node.attribute.sensorminnumcells: Only creatures with at least this number of cells are detected. Without a value there is no lower limit.
node.attribute.sensormaxnumcells: Only creatures with at most this number of cells are detected. Without a value there is no upper limit.
node.attribute.sensorrestricttolineage:
Restricts the detection to the relationship with the own creature.
 No: the lineage is not taken into account.
 Same lineage: only creatures of the own lineage are detected.
 Other lineage: only creatures of a foreign lineage are detected.
node.attribute.sensorminrange: Objects that are closer than this distance are not detected.
node.attribute.sensormaxrange: Objects that are farther away than this distance are not detected. The simulation parameter 'Radius' of the sensor cell type limits the range additionally.
node.attribute.generatoradditive: If enabled, the generated value is added to channel #0 instead of overwriting it.
node.attribute.generatorminvalue: Lower level of the generated signal.
node.attribute.generatormaxvalue: Upper level of the generated signal.
node.attribute.generatortimeoffset: Shifts the phase of the signal by this number of time steps.
node.attribute.generatormode:
Shape of the generated signal.
 Square signal: the maximum value is output in the first half of the period and the minimum value in the second half.
 Sawtooth signal: the output rises linearly from the minimum to the maximum value over the period.
node.attribute.generatorperiod: Length of one period in time steps.
node.attribute.attackermode:
Selects the targets of the attack. The stolen energy is added to the own raw energy.
 Free cell: steals energy from free cells within the attack radius.
 Creature: steals energy from cells of other creatures. Only creatures that a sensor cell of the same creature has detected and tagged in the current cycle are attacked.
node.attribute.attackerrestricttocolors: Only free cells with one of the selected customization colors are attacked.
node.attribute.injectorgeneindex: Gene index that is set in the constructor of the injected cell. It determines which gene is built there.
node.attribute.musclemode:
Selects how the muscle generates movement. Bending and crawling act on the first connection.
 Auto bending: bends back and forth on its own between the angle limits. Channel #1 sets the target direction.
 Manual bending: the bending direction follows the sign of channel #0.
 Angle bending: bends towards the direction given in channel #1 and turns the front direction along with it.
 Auto crawling: changes the connection length back and forth on its own.
 Manual crawling: the change of the connection length follows the sign of channel #0.
 Direct movement: accelerates the cell directly in the direction given in channel #1.
node.attribute.musclemaxangledeviation: Maximum deviation from the initial angle, as a fraction of the available angular range.
node.attribute.muscleforwardbackwardrati: Distributes the speed between the forward and the backward stroke. Since the faster stroke generates more thrust, this determines the direction of movement. At 0.5 both strokes cancel each other out.
node.attribute.muscleattractionrepulsion: Distributes the speed between the attracting and the repelling bending direction.
node.attribute.musclemaxdistancedeviatio: Maximum change of the connection length, relative to its initial value.
node.attribute.defendermode:
Selects against which foreign cells the creature is protected. Only the affected cell itself and its directly connected cells count.
 Anti-attacker: reduces the energy that attacker cells can steal from the own creature.
 Anti-injector: increases the energy cost for injector cells that target the own creature.
node.attribute.reconnectormode:
Selects the objects with which connections are established. A positive value in channel #0 creates a connection, a negative one removes all connections to objects that do not belong to the own creature.
 Solid: connections with solid particles.
 Free cell: connections with free cells.
 Creature: connections with cells of other creatures.
node.attribute.reconnectorrestricttocolo: Connections are only established with objects of the selected customization colors.
node.attribute.reconnectorminnumcells: Connections are only established with creatures that have at least this number of cells. Without a value there is no lower limit.
node.attribute.reconnectormaxnumcells: Connections are only established with creatures that have at most this number of cells. Without a value there is no upper limit.
node.attribute.reconnectorrestricttoline:
Restricts the connections to the relationship with the own creature.
 No: the lineage is not taken into account.
 Same lineage: connections only with creatures of the own lineage.
 Other lineage: connections only with creatures of a foreign lineage.
node.attribute.detonatorcountdown: Number of cycles until the explosion after the trigger. One cycle comprises 6 time steps.
node.attribute.digestorenergyconductivit: Determines how much raw energy the cell can take in from connected cells and pass on to connected digestor cells instead of converting it. It is scaled by the simulation parameter 'Max raw energy conductivity'. Complementary to 'Energy conversion'.
node.attribute.digestorenergyconversion: Determines how much raw energy the cell converts into usable energy per time step. It is scaled by the simulation parameter 'Max raw energy conversion'. Complementary to 'Energy conductivity'.
node.attribute.memorymode:
Selects how the signal is stored.
 Signal delay: outputs the signal again after a fixed number of cycles.
 Signal recorder: records the signal into the buffer or plays it back, controlled by the sign of channel #0.
 Signal storage: addresses one buffer entry via the absolute value of channel #0 and reads or overwrites it.
 Signal integrator: outputs a running average of the signal.
node.attribute.memorydelay: Number of cycles by which the signal is delayed. It also determines the size of the ring buffer.
node.attribute.memoryreadonly: If enabled, the cell only reads from the signal buffer and never overwrites it.
node.attribute.memorysignalbuffer: Opens the editor for the stored signal entries.
node.attribute.memorynewsignalweight: Weight of the current signal in the running average. At 0 the stored value is frozen, at 1 there is no smoothing.
node.attribute.memorychannelmask: Selects the channels that are overwritten with the stored values. The remaining channels are passed through unchanged.
node.attribute.communicatormode:
Selects the role in the communication. It only takes place between different creatures and requires a valid front direction on both sides.
 Send: transmits all own channels to the receivers in range. Requires a trigger via channel #0.
 Receive: takes over the channels of a sender. Channel #1 is converted into the own frame of reference.
node.attribute.communicatorrange: Radius within which receiver cells are addressed.
node.attribute.communicatoroneway: If enabled, only the receivers on one side are addressed, namely those opposite to the direction that is encoded in channel #1.
node.attribute.communicatorrestricttocol: Only signals from senders with one of the selected customization colors are accepted.
node.attribute.communicatorrestricttolin:
Restricts the reception to the relationship with the own creature.
 No: the lineage is not taken into account.
 Same lineage: only senders of the own lineage are accepted.
 Other lineage: only senders of a foreign lineage are accepted.
mutation.title: Mutation rates
mutation.resethelp: Reset all mutation rates to their default values. Adopt to apply the changes.
mutation.copyhelp: Copy all mutation rates to the clipboard
mutation.pastehelp: Paste all mutation rates from the clipboard
mutation.attribute.genomemutationratesed: Opens the editor for all mutation rates. The rows below only list the rates that are currently active.
mutation.attribute.genomemutationratessu: Opens the editor for all mutation rates. The number counts the mutation types with a probability above zero.
mutation.attribute.mutationconnectionpro: Probability per node and connection that the weight of that connection in the neural network is changed.
mutation.attribute.mutationconnectionval: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the connection weight. The result is limited to [-2, 2].
mutation.attribute.mutationneuronprobabi: Probability per node and neuron that the neuron is changed.
mutation.attribute.mutationneuronweightc: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of every input weight of the neuron. The result is limited to [-2, 2].
mutation.attribute.mutationneuronbiascha: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the bias of the neuron. The result is limited to [-2, 2].
mutation.attribute.mutationneuronactfnch: Probability that the activation function of the neuron is replaced by a randomly chosen one, which can also be the same.
mutation.attribute.mutationcelltypeprope: Probability per node that the properties of its cell type are changed.
Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the numeric properties, relative to the value range of each property.
Probability that a switch or a selection of the cell type properties is changed, such as a color or lineage restriction. The mode of the cell type is changed by a separate mutation.
mutation.attribute.mutationgeometryproba: Probability per gene that its geometry is changed.
mutation.attribute.mutationgeometryvalue: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the stiffness, relative to its value range. The connection distance is not mutated.
mutation.attribute.mutationgeometryenumc: Probability that the shape generator of the gene is replaced by a different one.
mutation.attribute.mutationcelltypemodep: Probability per node that the mode of its cell type is switched to a different one. The mode-specific properties are reset to their default values; cell types without a mode stay unchanged.
mutation.attribute.mutationcelltypeproba: Probability per node that its cell type is replaced by a different one, with all properties reset to their default values. Void nodes are not affected. With the same probability the switch 'Homogeneous cell type' of the gene is toggled.
mutation.attribute.mutationcustomization: Probability per genome that one used customization color is replaced everywhere by another one. Which replacements are permitted is defined by the simulation parameter 'Customization transition matrix'.
mutation.attribute.mutationvoidprobabili: Probability per node that it is toggled between void and a random other cell type. The first and the last node of a gene are not affected.
mutation.attribute.mutationextendgenepro: Probability per gene that a new node is appended at its beginning or at its end.
mutation.attribute.mutationaddnodeprobab: Probability per insertion position that a new node is inserted there.
mutation.attribute.mutationtrimgeneproba: Probability per gene that its first or its last node is removed. The last remaining node of a gene is always kept.
mutation.attribute.mutationdeletenodepro: Probability per node that it is removed. The last remaining node of a gene is always kept.
mutation.attribute.mutationaddgeneprobab: Probability per gene that a new gene consisting of a single node is created. A randomly chosen node of the triggering gene becomes a constructor that builds the new gene. Nodes whose cell type is void cannot become a constructor.
mutation.attribute.mutationduplicategene: Probability per gene that it is duplicated. Only genes that are referenced at least twice are duplicated; one of these references then points to the copy.
mutation.attribute.mutationdeletegenepro: Probability per gene that it is deleted. At least one gene is kept. A reference to a deleted gene switches off the referencing constructor and points a referencing injector to the first gene.
mutation.attribute.mutationswapgeneproba: Probability per gene that it is swapped with another randomly chosen gene. The gene indices stay the same, so every reference to one of the two genes now addresses the other one. A gene takes part in at most one swap per mutation pass.
mutation.attribute.mutationcopynodesecti: Probability per gene that a contiguous section of its nodes is copied into a randomly chosen gene, which can also be the gene itself.
mutation.attribute.mutationmovenodesecti: Probability per gene that a contiguous section of its nodes is moved into a randomly chosen gene. At least one node stays behind.
mutation.attribute.mutationconstructorpr: Probability per node that the constructor properties of the node are changed.
mutation.attribute.mutationconstructorva: Standard deviation of the Gaussian change of the numeric constructor properties, relative to the value range of each property.
mutation.attribute.mutationconstructoren: Probability that a switch or a selection of the constructor is changed.
mutation.attribute.mutationconstructorto: Probability that the constructor of the node is switched on or off.
genomeissues.meta: Meta-mutations may change the structural mutation rates, which decide whether the node gets a random cell type or the gene is removed.
genomeissues.cut.title: Nodes cut off from last node
genomeissues.cut.explanation: A construction stays attached to its constructor at the last node of a gene. Void cells die right after their construction, so nodes that are connected to the last node only via void nodes are lost. If the first node is among them, the whole gene is lost.
genomeissues.cut.void.one: {count} void node is cut off from the last node (index: {nodes}).
genomeissues.cut.void.few: {count} void nodes are cut off from the last node (indices: {nodes}).
genomeissues.cut.void.many: {count} void nodes are cut off from the last node (indices: {nodes}).
genomeissues.boundary.title: Void node at gene boundary
genomeissues.boundary.explanation: The first and the last node of a gene must not be void.
genomeissues.boundary.consequence: The node gets a random cell type.
genomeissues.cycle.title: Cycle avoiding the root gene
genomeissues.cycle.explanation: Constructors may only form cycles through the root gene, since constructing the root gene starts a new creature. A cycle avoiding the root gene would construct cells endlessly within the same creature.
genomeissues.unreachable.title: Gene unreachable from root
genomeissues.unreachable.problem: Not reachable from the root gene.
genomeissues.unreachable.followup: Becomes unreachable from the root gene.
genomeissues.unreachable.explanation: No chain of constructors leads from the root gene to this gene, so it is never constructed.
genomeissues.unreachable.cause: Another correction removes the last chain of constructors that leads from the root gene to this gene.
genomeissues.separation.title: Too many genes with separation
genomeissues.separation.problem: Constructs gene {target} with separation in addition to genes with indices {genes}.
genomeissues.separation.limit.one: At most {count} different gene can be constructed with separation. Genes are counted in construction order starting at the root gene.
genomeissues.separation.limit.few: At most {count} different genes can be constructed with separation. They are counted in construction order starting at the root gene.
genomeissues.separation.limit.many: At most {count} different genes can be constructed with separation. They are counted in construction order starting at the root gene.
genomeissues.separation.consequence: Separation is turned off, so gene {target} becomes part of the same creature.
genomeissues.constructs.title: Constructs a removed gene
genomeissues.constructs.explanation: The constructed gene is removed because of another warning.
genomeissues.injects.title: Injects a removed gene
genomeissues.injects.explanation: The injected gene is removed because of another warning.
genomeissues.injector: The injector uses the first remaining gene instead.
signals.title: Signal buffer
signals.counthelp: Set the number of stored signals.
signals.edithelp: Select the signal to edit by its index.
signals.channelhelp: Edit the value of this signal channel.
genomeissues.cut.empty: 0 void nodes are cut off from the last node.
genomeissues.cut.disconnect.one.one: Void node with index {voids} cuts node with index {nodes} off from the last node.
genomeissues.cut.disconnect.one.many: Void node with index {voids} cuts nodes with indices {nodes} off from the last node.
genomeissues.cut.disconnect.many.one: Void nodes with indices {voids} cut node with index {nodes} off from the last node.
genomeissues.cut.disconnect.many.many: Void nodes with indices {voids} cut nodes with indices {nodes} off from the last node.
